A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete supplementary material support comparison. Internal reporting inconsistencies in v2 limit interpretation of particular results, rather than material completeness.

before.justification: v1 reports original representation analyses, attention-knockout benchmark results, and activation-patching experiments in Section 4 and supplementary Sections 9–11.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical analyses and adds experiments involving Emu3, LLaVA, and Janus, reported in Section 4 and supplementary Section 6.

M1.justification: v2 introduces an actual model-adaptation step: LoRA fine-tuning of Emu3-Gen for image understanding before analysis (Sections 3.1 and SM7.1). The core cross-modal attention, neighborhood-overlap, knockout, and residual-patching tools remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds LLaVA-Instruct-150K to the data used for Emu3 fine-tuning, alongside VQAv2 and MS-COCO training data. Evaluation retains the same four datasets and task families: VQAv2, Flickr30k, MS-COCO, and ImageNet. The listed ImageNet classes are unchanged.

E2.justification: The comparison expands from Chameleon-7B/34B and Pixtral-12B to include adapted Emu3-8B, LLaVA-OneVision-7B, and Janus-1.3B. Pixtral remains evaluated in the appendix and gains explicit patching comparisons. The random-token ablation comparator is removed.

E3.justification: v2 introduces an Emu3 training protocol with one epoch, batch size 64, Adam, and cosine scheduling. It also reports progressive knockout on COCO using CIDEr in SM6.3, replacing v1's ImageNet neighborhood-overlap protocol in Section 4.3. This is a substantial reported protocol revision, although Figure SM3 retains neighborhood-overlap axis labels, leaving its plotted metric internally ambiguous.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands tests of whether localized communication generalizes across architectures, including negative patching results for LLaVA, Janus, and Pixtral. Progressive knockout is reworked and extended to Emu3 and LLaVA. Conversely, cumulative attention-input patching from v1 Figures 6 and A2, the random-token controls, and Pixtral's progressive-knockout curve are omitted.

E5.justification: v1 reports ten repetitions and standard deviation below 0.02 for random-token ablation; this reporting disappears with that control in v2. The shaded bands around v1's patching curves also disappear, although their statistical meaning was unspecified. Interquartile-range reporting for modality-gap plots and the ADP clustering significance procedure are retained.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for the additional models and revises retained-model scores. For example, Chameleon-7B Flickr/COCO CIDEr changes from 0.23/0.35 to 0.34/0.48 in Table 1, without explaining the revisions. The 90% patching statement aligns with v1 Figure A2, which already showed approximately that peak despite its 75% prose. Some v2 entries conflict: Chameleon-34B with [EOI] ablation scores 0.00 on ImageNet in Table 1 but 0.04 in Table SM2.

T1.justification: The substantive analytical definitions correspond directly between v1 Equations 2–4 and v2 Equations 1–3, and the ADP mathematical description is retained. v2 shortens the standard transformer background and clarifies patching accuracy without introducing substantive new mathematical reasoning, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The central narrow-gate, ablation, and steering contributions remain. v2 qualifies the broad multimodal-output generalization with 'tend to rely' in the abstract and explicitly recognizes Janus as a multimodal-output exception in the conclusion. The named localized-communication cases expand to include Emu3.

C2.justification: v2 adds an architecture-dependent interpretation: Janus suggests that text-aligned visual encoding and a text-pretrained backbone may suppress narrow gating. It also interprets Emu3's different depth dependence and adds implications concerning image-token removal for efficiency, localized alignment, and CLIP-like encoders as a possible safeguard. These substantially expand the mechanism hypotheses and applicability discussion.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies neighborhood-overlap k=30, Emu3 LoRA training settings including learning rate 5e-5, and detailed model configurations in Table SM3. Some earlier encoder and tokenization specifications are omitted. v2 also adds a release-upon-acceptance statement while retaining the code/data link; actual resource availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds a substantial related-work discussion contrasting visual encoders, diffusion decoders, discrete tokenization, contrastive alignment, and training from scratch. New references include BLIP-2, Cambrian-1, Janus, VILA-u, and work on the modality gap. This expands the architectural positioning beyond v1's emphasis on special tokens and information flow.

P1.justification: The model-description and methods sections are substantially reorganized, comparative results and the conclusion are rewritten, and the supplement is regrouped into Additional Results followed by Experimental Setup. These changes alter the narrative and organization beyond simply inserting experiments.

P2.justification: Figure 1 gains a quantitative ablation panel. Residual-patching similarity and accuracy panels from v1 Figures 6 and A2 are combined into v2 Figure 5, while cumulative-patching panels disappear. Pixtral displays move into expanded appendix figures, ablation tables are restructured, and Table SM3 adds an architecture comparison. Some captions remain inconsistent with their displays.

improvement.justification: v2 better establishes the architectural scope of narrow gating through additional models and the Janus counterexample, while adding useful implementation details. These gains strengthen and qualify the central conclusion. Their overall benefit is limited by removed controls and cumulative-patching evidence, unexplained score revisions, conflicting Table 1/SM2 entries, and Figure SM3's inconsistent metric labeling.
